sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for quashing of the order dated 30.07.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and the recovery certificate dated 12.01.2024 issued by respondent No.2 for recovery of the amount found to be due and payable by the petitioner under order dated 30.07.2022.
2.
The order dated 30.07.2022 was passed by the respondent No.2 on complaints filed by Gaurav Amlani, Lalit Prakash Amlani (respondent No.4) and Anita Amlani (wife of respondent No.4).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the three complaints were allowed and the petitioner (developer), who was impleaded as opposite party in the said proceedings, was directed to return the entire amount deposited by the complainants with it alongwith interest @ MCLR + 1% p.a.

In pursuance of the said order, recovery certificate dated 12.01.2024 for a sum of Rs.39,07,635.62/- has been issued in respect of the claim of respondent No.4.
3.

The submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that a First Information Report was lodged by the respondent No.4 against the petitioner under Sections 420, 406, 506 IPC in relation to the same transactions.

The directors of the petitioner company filed Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022 (Sageer Khan and 4 others vs. State of U.P. and 2 others) before this Court challenging the First Information Report.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sageer Khan and 4 others vs. State of U.P. and 2 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said proceedings, the petitioner handed over two bank drafts of Rs.25,48,842/- in the name of wife of respondent No.4 i.e. Smt. Anita Amlani.
It was alleged by the petitioner that it had paid a total sum of Rs.62,00,000/- and odd, which was also the amount mentioned in the First Information Report.
The said petition was entertained and an interim order was passed staying the investigation as well as consequential proceedings in pursuance of the First Information Report.

It is, thus, sought to be contended that the entire amount due and payable to respondent No.4 stood paid, however, respondent No.4 concealing the said fact has succeeded in getting the recovery certificate issued.

4. Shri Mohd. Afzal, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 submits that this Court, while granting stay in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022 has specifically noted the contention of respondent No.4 that dispute relating to non-payment of interest and certain other disputes remain unresolved and, therefore, left it open to respondent No.4 to raise the aforesaid claims in appropriate proceedings.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He submits that in view of the said liberty, there was no illegality in respondent No.4 praying for issuance of the recovery certificate and the same being issued by the respondent-Authority.
5. We have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the material placed on record.

6. The interim order passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022 specifically grants liberty to respondent No.4 that "in the event any further dispute survives it is always open for the informant to raise an appropriate claim in that regard".

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.5181 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: As noted, the wife of respondent No.4 had also filed a complaint based on allotment of a different flat in her favour.
It was also allowed by respondent No.2 by order dated 30.07.2022.

We have been informed that in pursuance of the said order, another recovery certificate dated 27.03.2024 was issued against the petitioner and, thereunder, a sum of Rs.52,48,185.66/- is payable by the petitioner to the wife of respondent No.4 and, as such, it cannot be said that the petitioner had cleared its entire liability so as to warrant quashing of the impugned order or the recovery certificate issued pursuant thereto.

7. We, therefore, decline to interfere with the impugned order as well as the recovery certificate but leave it open to the petitioner to bring complete facts including the one with regard to payment of Rs.62,00,000/- and odd by it to the wife of respondent No.4 before respondent No.2 so that respondent No.2 may work out the amount which is still due and payable to respondent No.4 and Archmate Samiah Consortium vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190505060/
2

8. Subject to the above observations, the petition is disposed of.
